## Pull request overview

This PR integrates the `PageCanvasEditor` and `DashboardEditor` designer components from `@object-ui/plugin-designer` into the Console application, enabling full WYSIWYG editing of pages and dashboards. The integration follows the established lazy-loading pattern for route-based code splitting and provides a complete editing experience with auto-save, keyboard shortcuts, JSON export/import, and edit button entry points from read-only views.

**Changes:**
- Added two new design routes (`/design/page/:pageName` and `/design/dashboard/:dashboardName`) that wrap the editor components with save logic, keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+S), and export/import handlers
- Added Edit buttons to `PageView` and `DashboardView` that navigate to the corresponding design routes using relative paths
- Created Storybook stories for both editor components with Default, WithComponents/WithWidgets, and ReadOnly variants

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 11 out of 11 changed files in this pull request and generated 13 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `packages/plugin-designer/src/PageCanvasEditor.stories.tsx` | New Storybook stories for PageCanvasEditor with 3 variants (Default, WithComponents, ReadOnly) |
| `packages/plugin-designer/src/DashboardEditor.stories.tsx` | New Storybook stories for DashboardEditor with 3 variants (Default, WithWidgets, ReadOnly) |
| `apps/console/src/pages/PageDesignPage.tsx` | New page component wrapping PageCanvasEditor with auto-save, Ctrl+S shortcut, export/import handlers, and 404 handling |
| `apps/console/src/pages/DashboardDesignPage.tsx` | New page component wrapping DashboardEditor with auto-save, Ctrl+S shortcut, export/import handlers, and 404 handling |
| `apps/console/src/components/PageView.tsx` | Added Edit button in hover-revealed toolbar that navigates to design route |
| `apps/console/src/components/DashboardView.tsx` | Added Edit button in header that navigates to design route |
| `apps/console/src/__tests__/console-load-performance.test.tsx` | Updated MAX_CHUNK_COUNT from 20 to 22 to account for two new lazy-loaded design pages |
| `apps/console/src/__tests__/PageDesignPage.test.tsx` | New test file with 6 tests covering rendering, 404, back navigation, schema passthrough, onChange, and Ctrl+S save |
| `apps/console/src/__tests__/DashboardDesignPage.test.tsx` | New test file with 6 tests covering rendering, 404, back navigation, schema passthrough, onChange, and Ctrl+S save |
| `apps/console/src/App.tsx` | Added lazy imports for design pages, registered routes, and excluded 'design' from objectNameFromPath detection |
| `ROADMAP.md` | Updated console integration section with design page features, Ctrl+S shortcut, Storybook story count (78→80), and test counts |
</details>

The keyboard event listener for Ctrl+S is attached to the global window object without checking if the user is focused on an input element or contenteditable area. This means pressing Ctrl+S while typing in a text field within the PageCanvasEditor will trigger a save, which could be disruptive to the user's workflow. Consider adding a check to prevent the shortcut from firing when the user is typing, similar to the pattern used in KeyboardShortcutsDialog.tsx where it checks if the target is an input, textarea, or contenteditable element.

This means pressing Ctrl+S while typing in a text field within the DashboardEditor will trigger a save, which could be disruptive to the user's workflow. The Edit button lacks an aria-label attribute. While the button has visible text ("Edit") and an icon, adding an explicit aria-label would improve accessibility for screen reader users by providing clearer context, such as "Edit page" or "Edit page {pageName}". This is especially important since the button appears in a hover-revealed toolbar where context might not be immediately clear.

The Edit button lacks an aria-label attribute. While the button has visible text ("Edit") and an icon, adding an explicit aria-label would improve accessibility for screen reader users by providing clearer context, such as "Edit dashboard" or "Edit dashboard {dashboardName}". This is especially important for providing clear context about what is being edited.

The tests do not include cleanup logic (afterEach or cleanup() calls) to unmount components and remove event listeners after each test. Since the PageDesignPage component attaches a global keydown listener to window, running multiple tests in sequence may leave stale event listeners attached, potentially causing test interference or false positives. Consider adding afterEach cleanup or using @testing-library/react's cleanup utility to ensure each test starts with a clean state.

The tests do not include cleanup logic (afterEach or cleanup() calls) to unmount components and remove event listeners after each test. Since the DashboardDesignPage component attaches a global keydown listener to window, running multiple tests in sequence may leave stale event listeners attached, potentially causing test interference or false positives. Consider adding afterEach cleanup or using @testing-library/react's cleanup utility to ensure each test starts with a clean state.

The component initializes schema state with a fallback value even when the page is not found (line 27), but then returns early with a 404 message (lines 91-97). This means the state initialization, useCallback hooks, and useEffect hook all execute even when the page doesn't exist. While functionally harmless since the 404 UI is returned before rendering the editor, this pattern wastes computation. Consider moving the early return check before state initialization and hook declarations, or use a loading state pattern to defer hook execution until page existence is confirmed.

The component initializes schema state with a fallback value even when the dashboard is not found (lines 26-35), but then returns early with a 404 message (lines 98-104). This means the state initialization, useCallback hooks, and useEffect hook all execute even when the dashboard doesn't exist. While functionally harmless since the 404 UI is returned before rendering the editor, this pattern wastes computation. Consider moving the early return check before state initialization and hook declarations, or use a loading state pattern to defer hook execution until dashboard existence is confirmed.

The saveSchema function swallows all errors silently without logging or providing feedback to the user. When auto-save fails, users have no indication that their changes weren't persisted. Consider adding at minimum a console.error for debugging and optionally a toast.error for user notification, while still allowing retry via export as noted in the comment.

The PageDesignPage and DashboardDesignPage components contain significant code duplication. They share identical patterns for: state management (schema + schemaRef), save logic, keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+S), export/import handlers, 404 rendering, header layout with back button, and editor wrapping structure. Consider extracting a generic DesignPageWrapper component or a custom hook (useDesignPageLogic) to reduce duplication and improve maintainability. The wrapper could accept the schema type, editor component, entity name, and metadata accessor as parameters.
